title: Advanced Dynamic Programming
relevance: Hard SDE OAs use advanced DP to test whether candidates can reshape state for trees, subsets, digit ranges, and intervals beyond classic 1D/2D tables.

phases.goal: Establish that advanced DP is still state + recurrence + memoization, with the state shape as the main change.

must_hit.point: Every advanced DP still follows define the state, write the recurrence, and memoize.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate says advanced paradigms do not change the core DP process—only how the state is shaped.

must_hit.point: Advanced state shapes include a bitmask of visited items, a boolean tight flag in digit DP, or multi-value returns from child subtrees in tree DP.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions at least two concrete shapes (bitmask, tight, or tree child returns) as examples of state design.

must_hit.point: Tree DP often requires a node to return multiple pieces of information to its parent, typically as a pair or struct of states.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says returning a pair/struct cleanly encapsulates subproblem results for the parent.

probes: What stays the same across advanced DP paradigms, and what actually changes?
Give examples of unusual DP state shapes beyond a simple index into an array.

hints.1: Start from ordinary DP: state, transition, memo—what part of that story changes here?
hints.2: Contrast a classic dp[i] with tree returns, subset masks, and digit construction flags.
hints.3: Answer: same define-state / recurrence / memoize loop; state may be a bitmask, tight boolean, or multi-field tree return.

phases.goal: Check how tree, bitmask, digit, and interval DP actually iterate and define transitions.

must_hit.point: Tree DP typically runs post-order DFS: each node gets children's DP results, combines them into its own state, and returns that to its parent.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes children-first recursion, combine at node, return upward.

must_hit.point: In bitmask DP the i-th bit of mask is 1 iff the i-th item is in the subset, enabling memoization over all 2^n subsets; it is typically viable only when n ≤ 20.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Explains bit encoding of membership and the n ≤ 20 viability bound.

must_hit.point: Digit DP counts valid numbers in [L, R] via f(R) − f(L − 1); the tight flag means choices are constrained by X when true, and free digits 0–9 when false.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States the range reduction and correctly explains tight vs non-tight digit limits.

must_hit.point: Interval DP uses state dp[left][right] and almost always iterates by interval length from 2 to n.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names left/right state and length-increasing iteration order.

probes: Walk through how a tree DP node obtains and returns its state.
How do you encode subsets in bitmask DP, and when is that approach viable?
What does the tight flag mean when building a number digit by digit?

hints.1: Pick one paradigm and describe the loop or DFS order before naming formulas.
hints.2: Tree: post-order; bitmask: bits as membership; digit: left-to-right with a bound flag; interval: grow by length.
hints.3: Post-order combine-and-return; mask bit i means item i included, n ≤ 20; f(R)−f(L−1) with tight limiting the digit; dp[left][right] by length 2..n.

phases.goal: Judge when each advanced DP flavour is the right tool and what state-design choices buy you.

must_hit.point: Bitmask DP fits when n ≤ 20 and the problem involves permutations, subsets, or assignments; digit DP is the tool for counting numbers in a range with property P; tree DP when aggregating over a rooted tree (paths or subset selections); interval DP when collapsing adjacent elements and operation order matters.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Maps each flavour to its trigger: small-n subsets, range digit properties, rooted-tree aggregation, adjacent collapse with order.

must_hit.point: For TSP, brute-force permutations are O(n!) while DP over dp[mask][u] is O(n^2 2^n) time and O(n 2^n) space.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Contrasts factorial enumeration with the mask×city DP complexities from the file.

must_hit.point: With n ≤ 10 people and hats ≤ 40, masking people (not hats) is vastly more efficient for hat-assignment counting.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Chooses the smaller dimension for the bitmask and cites the people vs hats size contrast.

probes: When would you reach for bitmask vs digit vs tree vs interval DP?
Why not mask over hats in the different-hats counting problem?

hints.1: Ask what the input size and structure force: tiny n, digit ranges, trees, or adjacent merges.
hints.2: Recall the close guidance: n ≤ 20 subsets; count-in-range digits; rooted-tree aggregates; collapsing adjacent with order.
hints.3: Bitmask n ≤ 20; digit for range property counts; tree for rooted aggregation; interval for ordered adjacent collapse; hat problem masks people because n ≤ 10 vs hats ≤ 40.

phases.goal: Apply state design on concrete hard problems: path/tree choices, subset tours/assignments, digit counts, and last-burst intervals.

must_hit.point: In binary-tree maximum path sum, the arch through a node is node.val + max(0, left) + max(0, right), but the value returned to the parent may include at most one child path: node.val + max(0, max(left, right)).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Separates global arch update (both sides) from the single-branch return to the parent.

must_hit.point: House Robber III state at a node is the pair {max if not robbed, max if robbed}; rob forces children not-robbed, skip takes max of each child's options.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States the two-valued return and the rob vs skip child constraints.

must_hit.point: Binary Tree Cameras classifies nodes as 0 has camera, 1 covered, 2 needs cover; place a camera if any child is 2, become covered if any child is 0, else return 2; if the root returns 2, place one more camera.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Lists the three states, the child-driven transitions, and the root edge case.

must_hit.point: In Burst Balloons, decide the last balloon k burst in (left, right) so subproblems (left, k) and (k, right) are independent; first-burst thinking couples the sides.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Explains last-burst independence versus first-burst dependence across the cut.

probes: In maximum path sum, what do you update globally versus what do you return upward?
How do you encode rob/skip at a house in the tree, and what may children do in each case?
Why think about the last balloon to burst in an interval rather than the first?

hints.1: Distinguish information needed for a path through the node from a valid continuation to the parent.
hints.2: Path sum: both children for the arch, one child on return; robber: pair of robbed/not; balloons: last k shields left and right.
hints.3: Arch = val+max(0,L)+max(0,R), return = val+max(0,max(L,R)); pair {not robbed, robbed}; last burst k makes (left,k) and (k,right) independent.

tradeoffs.topic: Brute permutations vs bitmask DP for TSP
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Enumerating city permutations is O(n!); DP with state dp[mask][u] (visited set plus current city) runs in O(n^2 2^n) time and O(n 2^n) space.

tradeoffs.topic: Mask people vs mask hats for different-hat assignments
tradeoffs.strong_answer: With n ≤ 10 people and hats ≤ 40, a bitmask over people (iterating hats 1..40) is vastly cheaper than masking hats.

tradeoffs.topic: First balloon vs last balloon as the interval split
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Choosing the first balloon to burst couples the two sides; choosing the last balloon k in (left, right) makes (left, k) and (k, right) independent until k bursts.

tradeoffs.topic: Which advanced DP flavour to use
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Bitmask when n ≤ 20 with permutations/subsets/assignments; digit DP for counting numbers in a range with property P; tree DP to aggregate over a rooted tree (paths or subset selections); interval DP when collapsing adjacent elements and order of operations matters.

gotchas.trap: Returning both children's contributions from a node in maximum path sum as if that were a valid parent continuation.
gotchas.correction: The arch through the node may use both sides for the global answer, but the return to the parent may include at most one child path so it remains a single path.

gotchas.trap: Storing which person is being assigned explicitly in the assignment-problem DP state.
gotchas.correction: The number of set bits in the assigned-task mask (__builtin_popcount) already identifies person k; only the task mask is needed.

gotchas.trap: Placing cameras greedily on leaves, or forgetting the root when it still needs cover.
gotchas.correction: Prefer covering a leaf via its parent; after post-order, if the root returns needs-cover (2), place one more camera. Null children are treated as covered (1).

gotchas.trap: In digit DP, treating leading zeros as used digits for uniqueness, or forgetting the tight constraint.
gotchas.correction: Track isLeadingZero so leading zeros do not mark digits used; when tight is true the digit limit is the bound digit, otherwise 0–9.

gotchas.trap: Ignoring negative downward paths in tree path problems by always adding child sums.
gotchas.correction: Take max(0, child_path) so a negative extension is dropped rather than forced into the path.
